hard_constraints: no action grants hierarchy-derived cross-scope authority
no action operates voting-domain key material or ballot content
every mutation requires commit-time reauthorization and immutable evidence

no_ui_decisions.rationale: The Voting Client and the voting trust domain remain outside every administrative control-plane surface (FIR-CTRL-001 acceptance criterion 7). Trustee key authority is exercised only through voting-domain components under voting-specific governance.
Voting-domain key material appears in the control plane only as an external governed reference (FIR-SEC-004 class 9). No control-plane right operates it.
Deliberately does not exist. There is no console, desk, role or route that aggregates the full right set (FIR-CTRL-001 acceptance criterion 9).

actions.notes: A human review decision is mandatory; the model never holds the execute right.
Read-only by construction: the audit desk holds no mutation right on any object class.
Assignment must cite the source election/appointment decision and rule version.
Read model. Summarises current state without erasing historical source records.
A technical administrator cannot restore a politically suspended office.
FIR-GOV-004 level 2. Suspension fails authorization at the moment of every affected act.
Recovery restores the ability to authenticate. It never restores a suspended OrganizationalAuthority.
The authenticator generates the private key; the platform registers only public material.
Never resurrects a revoked credential under the same identity; replacement links forward.
Nomination, filing and election administration are separately authorised; no ballot access.
Activation sets an absolute expiry. There is no renewal path.
Approver must be distinct from the requester; the controller is a separate principal.
Mandatory post-use review. The reviewer may not be an actor of the reviewed grant.
prepare / approve / execute / book / review are separable per scope.
Level 2. Requires the competent organ chain and a confirmation route.
Level 3. Freezes named action codes only; a scope-wide disable is prohibited.
Level 1 containment may be pre-authorised by incident policy; it is not a removal from office.
Level 4. Bounded at 90 days; extension requires a new decision.
Retention and decryption-dependency check precedes destruction; no export before destroy.
Stops new use. Grants no right to inspect unrelated secrets.
Approver and auditor need no plaintext material; high-impact classes require quorum.
Party office and public mandate remain distinct; neither derives the other.
Privacy-safe operational state only. Deploy/restart authority grants no domain authority.
Workload-only action. A human principal is refused on actor-class grounds.
Commercial operations boundary: a vendor engagement creates no party competence.
Retention application never removes audit evidence of the act itself.
Separately protected custody; not reachable from ordinary investigation authority.
Delivery is machine-bound. Approval never requires plaintext secret visibility.
Immediate containment may be pre-authorised; replacement activation follows full SoD.
Publication authority is confined to the actor's own official scope.
